evidence.source: 中央研究院小學堂文字學資料庫
evidence.text: The entry displays 肉 across oracle-bone, Chu bamboo-and-silk, and small-seal categories, and describes the ancient graph as shaped like a piece of meat. The accessible text does not give dates for individual specimens or document a full sequence of graphic changes.
evidence.title: 漢字「肉」：字形演變

evidence.text: Xu Shen glosses 肉 as 胾肉 and classifies it as pictographic. The received annotation interprets 胾 as a large piece of animal meat and says 肉 was extended to the body of a ring-shaped object and to the “flesh” of music. These are dictionary explanations, not independently dated attestations of each sense.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary entry and later annotation
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.text: The entry gives citations for meat and bodily flesh from transmitted works including Zuǒzhuàn, Mèngzǐ, Xúnzǐ, Mòzǐ, and Zhànguócè, but does not establish the date of the cited wording or the earliest use of each sense. It separately lists fruit pulp with a citation from 齊民要術 and the ring-body sense with citations from 爾雅 and 漢書 commentary. These should not be collapsed into a single chronology from the modern gloss list.
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.field: 音韻方言／上古音；local primary reading rows
evidence.text: 漢典 lists modern Mandarin ròu and Tang reading *njiuk, and gives broad Old Chinese labels from Huang Kan and Wang Li without a single transcription. The supplied local Unihan row records 肉 kMandarin ròu; the supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 row records 肉 MC nyuwk and OC *k.nuk. These systems are distinct. Unicode's official character page could not be accessed in this research session, so the local rows are reported as supplied local data, not as externally verified evidence.
evidence.kind: pronunciation metadata; local primary rows noted
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.field: 異體字研訂／形體資料表
evidence.text: The entry treats 宍 and 𠕎 as graphic variants of 肉 and discusses their later written history. For 𠕎 it says the form derives through clerical transformation from the Shuowen seal form. This supports a variant relationship for those forms, but not an oracle-bone-to-modern sequence in detail.
evidence.title: [A03288] 肉 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

gaps: The separate Commons File:Shuowen Seal Radical 135.svg page and its exact original URL could not be opened or verified. The page's identity, image content, provenance, and license therefore remain unverified; do not select or caption this image as inspected evidence.

The Han Dian entry lists oracle-bone specimens and Academia Sinica lists script categories, but accessible text did not date particular 肉 attestations or provide a detailed, critically argued sequence of shape changes. No glyph image was visually inspected here.

No inspected source established a whole-graph phonetic borrowing for 肉. Etymological proposals in the dossier about Proto-Sino-Tibetan roots remain unverified here; the pictographic graph claim does not by itself settle the spoken word's deeper etymology.

Earliest attested uses and the chronological links among animal meat, bodily flesh, fruit pulp, ring-body, musical timbre, and other extended senses remain undetermined from the inspected evidence. The dictionary citations are not a dated corpus survey.

The official Unicode Unihan character page was attempted but inaccessible. The task's supplied local kMandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows are identified as local data, not external citations; no external click-through evidence for those exact rows was verified.
